sources.source: Building Permits Survey, county annual files (U.S. Census Bureau)
sources.version: 1990-2025 annual files (the 2025 file is the latest published)
sources.cleaning: Two header rows are joined and columns are read by name, not position. Reported and imputed figures are kept apart. County FIPS codes are zero-padded to five digits.
sources.limits: Counts units authorized by permit, not units started or finished. Some counties are imputed rather than reported; the file flags which. Places without permit offices are not covered.

sources.source: American Community Survey 5-year table-based summary files (2020-2024) (U.S. Census Bureau)
sources.cleaning: Rows are filtered to the state's tracts by GEO_ID prefix. Negative missing-value codes become blanks. Estimates (E) and margins of error (M) are both kept.
sources.limits: Estimates are survey averages over five years with margins of error; small tracts often have wide margins. One national pipe-delimited file per table (about 48 MB for B25024). Negative values are missing-value codes, not data.

sources.source: American Community Survey 5-year estimates via the Census Data API (2020-2024) (U.S. Census Bureau)
sources.licence: Public domain (U.S. government work); API terms of service apply
sources.cleaning: Same as the summary files. Variable labels are checked against the vintage's variable list before use.
sources.limits: At most 50 variables per call. On 2026-11-22 a call without a key was answered with a "Missing Key" page, so this path needs CENSUS_API_KEY; the summary-file path above needs no key and gives the same estimates.

sources.source: Cartographic boundary file, census tracts, 2020, 1:500,000 (U.S. Census Bureau)
sources.cleaning: Shapes are simplified further and written as small GeoJSON files per county.
sources.limits: Generalized (simplified) shapes for maps, not for measuring land area or for parcel work. 2020 tracts match the 2020-2024 ACS.

sources.source: Cartographic boundary file, counties, 2020, 1:500,000 (U.S. Census Bureau)
sources.cleaning: Filtered to the state, simplified, written as GeoJSON.
sources.limits: One national file; generalized shapes for maps only.

sources.source: TIGER/Line 2020 tabulation blocks (attribute table only) (U.S. Census Bureau)
sources.cleaning: Keeps GEOID20, HOUSING20, POP20, ALAND20, AWATER20 and the internal point.
sources.limits: Housing units and population are 2020 counts, not current. Internal points are a point inside each block, not its centre of population. Only the attribute table (the .dbf, about 46 MB of the 409 MB Pennsylvania zip) is read, by HTTP range requests; block shapes are never downloaded.

sources.source: FHFA House Price Index, annual, counties (Federal Housing Finance Agency)
sources.cleaning: Converted to long form (county, year, index, annual change). Missing years stay missing.
sources.limits: Repeat-sales index built from mortgages bought or guaranteed by Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac; thin in rural counties, where years can be missing. Published as a spreadsheet (read with the standard library's zip and XML tools).

sources.source: FHFA House Price Index, annual, census tracts (Federal Housing Finance Agency)
sources.cleaning: Filtered to the state's tracts. Missing values stay missing.
sources.limits: Experimental tract-level index; many tracts have too few repeat sales and are blank. Check which tract vintage (2010 or 2020) each release uses before joining.

sources.source: Primary Mortgage Market Survey, weekly rate history (Freddie Mac)
sources.licence: Published freely by Freddie Mac; use under its website terms, with attribution
sources.cleaning: Weekly 30-year and 15-year fixed rates; an annual average is computed.
sources.limits: National average offered rates for prime borrowers, not the rate a given household or builder pays. The value used in the model is a ledger parameter with a range.

sources.source: HUD Fair Market Rents, county and metro area file (U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development)
sources.cleaning: Rents by bedroom count per county; metro-wide values are applied to member counties.
sources.limits: Fair Market Rents are the 40th percentile of recent movers' gross rents, set for voucher payments; they are a cross-check, not a market rent. The direct file is used, never the token-gated API.
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development

sources.source: National Transit Map, stops (U.S. Department of Transportation, Bureau of Transportation Statistics)
sources.version: National Transportation Atlas Database release compiled 2026-09-23
sources.cleaning: Keeps stop id, name, latitude, longitude, stop type and feed id. Stops with no pickup are excluded later, using the agency feeds.
sources.limits: Stops as reported by agencies in their schedule feeds; some agencies are missing or out of date. Gives stop locations, not service frequency (frequency comes from the agency schedule feeds). About 673,000 stops nationally; queried by state bounding box in pages of at most 2,000.
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, Bureau of Transportation Statistics

sources.source: Pennsylvania House Bill 2186 (accessory dwelling units), bill page and text (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
sources.cleaning: Only status, dates and cited sections are recorded, in a hand-checked rule file.
sources.limits: A proposed bill, not law, unless enacted; it lapses at the end of the session. Status is re-checked after November 30.

sources.source: Pennsylvania Senate Bill 1346 (accessory dwelling units), bill page and text (Pennsylvania General Assembly)
sources.cleaning: Only status, dates and cited sections are recorded, in a hand-checked rule file.
sources.limits: A proposed bill, not law, unless enacted. Applies only to municipalities under the Municipalities Planning Code, so not to Philadelphia or Pittsburgh.

sources.source: Building Permits Survey, state annual files (U.S. Census Bureau)
sources.version: 1990-2025 annual files (the 2025 file is the latest published)
sources.cleaning: Same header rules as the county files. Region, division and U.S. total rows are dropped. Value is converted to dollars.
sources.limits: State totals of units authorized by permit, including the Bureau's imputation for offices that did not report. Construction value is in thousands of dollars.

sources.source: American Community Survey 5-year summary file geography list (2020-2024) (U.S. Census Bureau)
sources.cleaning: Streamed; only the state's state, county and tract rows are written to disk. The national file is never stored.
sources.limits: One national pipe-delimited file (about 91 MB) that names every geography in the summary files. Tracts are 2020 census tracts.

sources.source: American Community Survey 5-year table shells (2020-2024) (U.S. Census Bureau)
sources.cleaning: Streamed; only the rows of the tables used are written to disk.
sources.limits: The label of every table cell for this vintage; it holds no estimates.

sources.source: Quarterly Census of Employment and Wages, annual averages, construction (NAICS 23) (U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics)
sources.cleaning: Streamed; only the state's rows and the national row are written to disk. Private ownership (code 5) at nation, state and county level is kept. County pay is divided by state pay to give a county wage index.
sources.limits: Average pay of construction jobs at private employers, by where the employer reports, not where it builds. A wage index is a proxy for local building costs; materials, land and fees are not in it. BLS withholds county figures that would reveal one employer; those counties take the state value.

sources.source: National Transit Map, agencies (U.S. Department of Transportation, Bureau of Transportation Statistics)
sources.version: National Transportation Atlas Database release compiled 2026-09-23
sources.cleaning: Keeps the National Transit Database id and agency name of the agencies with stops in the state's bounding box.
sources.limits: Agency names and addresses only; used to label the transit coverage table.
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Transportation, Bureau of Transportation Statistics

sources.source: Mobility Database catalog of transit schedule feeds (MobilityData)
sources.licence: Catalog published openly by MobilityData; each listed feed keeps its agency's own terms
sources.cleaning: Keeps the state's schedule (GTFS) feeds. A deprecated feed is used only when the same provider has no active one.
sources.limits: A volunteer-maintained list; some agencies are missing, listed under another state, or listed only with an old (deprecated) feed. Feeds that need a key or log-in are not used.

sources.source: Transit agency schedule feeds (GTFS), via their published addresses or the catalog mirror (Each transit agency (copies mirrored by MobilityData))
sources.version: The schedule current when fetched; the representative date is recorded per feed
sources.licence: Each agency's own open-data terms (for example SEPTA and Pittsburgh Regional Transit developer terms)
sources.cleaning: Reads stops, routes, trips, stop times, calendars and frequencies (never shapes). Counts boarding calls per stop on the busiest Tuesday to Thursday; a trip's last stop and no-pickup calls are left out. Only the per-stop counts are stored.
sources.limits: Scheduled, not actual, service. One representative weekday per feed. Only feeds that download without a key are used; bus stops of other agencies are marked frequency unknown. Agencies change stop ids between schedules, so a few stops may not match the National Transit Map.
sources.publisher: Each transit agency (copies mirrored by MobilityData)

sources.source: LEHD Origin-Destination Employment Statistics (LODES 8), workplace area characteristics, all jobs (U.S. Census Bureau, Longitudinal Employer-Household Dynamics program)
sources.cleaning: Block rows are summed to 2020 tracts: total jobs, three monthly-earnings bands and 20 industry sectors. Only the tract sums are kept; the block file is deleted.
sources.limits: Counts jobs covered by unemployment insurance plus federal civilian jobs, by where people work. Self-employed people, the military and informal work are not counted. A person with two jobs counts twice. The Census Bureau adds noise to block counts for privacy; tract and county sums are much steadier.
sources.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau, Longitudinal Employer-Household Dynamics program

sources.source: LEHD Origin-Destination Employment Statistics (LODES 8), home-to-work flows, all jobs (U.S. Census Bureau, Longitudinal Employer-Household Dynamics program)
sources.cleaning: Streamed line by line; jobs (S000) are summed to pairs of counties (work county, home county or "out_of_state"). Only the county pairs are kept.
sources.limits: Links each job's workplace block to the worker's home block. The "main" file covers jobs with both ends in the state; the "aux" file adds workers who live in another state. Residents who work in another state are in that state's files, which are not read, so out-commuting across the state line is not counted. Same job coverage as the workplace file.
sources.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau, Longitudinal Employer-Household Dynamics program

sources.source: County Business Patterns, county file (U.S. Census Bureau)
sources.cleaning: The national zip is read as a stream; the state's all-sector and two-digit NAICS sector rows are kept. Payroll stays in thousands of dollars. The zip is deleted.
sources.limits: Counts private establishments with paid employees and their mid-March employment and yearly payroll. Government, self-employed and most farm work are left out. Small cells carry noise; the noise flag is kept. Establishments that cannot be placed in a county are left out, so counties do not add up to the state total.

sources.source: Low-Income Housing Tax Credit Qualified Census Tracts (U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development)
sources.version: HUD's latest designations (map item titled 2027, updated 2026-10-28; 2020 tracts)
sources.cleaning: Keeps the 11-digit tract code of every designated tract in the state (attributes only, no shapes).
sources.limits: A Qualified Census Tract lets a tax-credit project claim a 30% larger basis. Designations change every year; HUD's map item and layer text name different years (2026 and 2027), so the edition is stated as published. Being in a QCT does not mean a project will get credits.
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development

sources.source: Low-Income Housing Tax Credit Difficult Development Areas (U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development)
sources.version: HUD's latest designations (map item titled 2027, updated 2026-10-28)
sources.cleaning: Keeps every DDA's ZCTA or county code and type (SA = small-area metro, NM = non-metro county); attributes only.
sources.limits: In metro areas, Difficult Development Areas are ZIP Code Tabulation Areas (ZCTAs); outside them, whole counties. A tract is matched to ZCTAs by shared land area, so a tract on a ZCTA edge can be partly in a DDA.
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development

sources.source: 2020 ZIP Code Tabulation Area to census tract relationship file (U.S. Census Bureau)
sources.cleaning: Streamed; only rows whose tract is in the state are kept (ZCTA, tract, shared land area).
sources.limits: Land area shared by each ZCTA and tract; used only to place ZCTA-based DDAs on tracts.

sources.source: Qualified Opportunity Zones designated for 2027 (second decennial round) (U.S. Department of the Treasury)
sources.cleaning: Keeps the state's tracts and the rural flag.
sources.limits: The new round of zones starts on 2027-01-01. The first-round zones (2018, on 2010 tracts) end on 2026-12-31 and are not shown. Treasury says taxpayers may not rely on the web list to support a tax position.

sources.source: New Markets Tax Credit low-income community tracts (2016-2020 ACS) (U.S. Department of the Treasury, CDFI Fund)
sources.version: 2016-2020 ACS eligibility file released 2023-09-01 (required for investments closed from 2024-09-01)
sources.cleaning: Read with a small standard-library reader for Excel binary (.xlsb) files; keeps the state's tracts, the yes/no test results, the poverty rate and the income percentage. The national file is deleted.
sources.limits: Shows whether a tract meets the poverty (20% or more) or income (80% of the benchmark or less) test. Other routes to eligibility (high-migration rural counties, targeted populations) are not shown. The CDFI Fund does not update the file every year.
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of the Treasury, CDFI Fund

sources.source: Low-Income Housing Tax Credit properties (HUD LIHTC database) (U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development)
sources.version: HUD LIHTC map service updated 2026-04-20; Pennsylvania projects placed in service through 2020
sources.cleaning: Keeps id, units, low-income units, year placed in service (8888/9999 = unknown), county code and latitude/longitude. Points are placed in 2020 tracts by their coordinates.
sources.limits: Projects placed in service since 1987 as reported by state agencies; recent years are incomplete (the map service's Pennsylvania records stop at 2020) and the year is unknown for some projects. A project's point is the address of its largest building. Projects that left the program are not removed.
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development

sources.source: Keystone Opportunity Zone (KOZ) locations, public view (Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development)
sources.licence: Public Commonwealth map layer; no licence stated
sources.cleaning: Keeps county name, acreage, developed and occupied flags, expiry year and the point; personal contact fields are dropped.
sources.limits: Pennsylvania only. The sites DCED lists on its public KOZ map, with acreage and expiry year; it may not hold every active KOZ parcel. Contact names on the layer are not kept.
sources.publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development

sources.source: National Register of Historic Places, listed property points and polygons (U.S. Department of the Interior, National Park Service)
sources.cleaning: Keeps reference number, type, status and location of listed properties in the state. District polygons are simplified to about 10 metres.
sources.limits: Only properties NPS has mapped and does not restrict are shown, so counts are a floor. A district polygon's homes are 2020 Census block homes whose block centre is inside it. Listing makes income-producing rehabilitation eligible for the federal historic tax credit; it does not grant one.
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of the Interior, National Park Service

sources.source: FBI Crime Data Explorer API, agency list and agency offense counts (summary reporting) (U.S. Department of Justice, Federal Bureau of Investigation)
sources.licence: Public domain (U.S. government work); the API needs a free api.data.gov key
sources.cleaning: Sums each local and State Police agency's monthly violent and property offenses for the year; keeps agencies that reported all twelve months; adds them by county with the populations they serve.
sources.limits: Offenses known to police, as agencies report them; not victimization. Coverage depends on which agencies reported all twelve months. Pennsylvania moved to the incident-based system (NIBRS) around 2021, so counts before and after the change are not comparable. Agencies are placed in counties by the FBI's agency list; an agency serving several counties is counted in the first one. No tract figures.
sources.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Federal Bureau of Investigation

sources.source: Municipal Statistics, County / Municipal Planning, Zoning & Building Code report (Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development (DCED))
sources.version: current (the report is kept up to date by DCED)
sources.licence: Public information published by a Pennsylvania state agency; no licence stated. Cited as "PA DCED Municipal Statistics".
sources.cleaning: The ASP.NET form is posted for all counties and the report exported as CSV. County government rows are dropped. Yes/no answers become 1/0; the lists of member municipalities become counts. Matched to Census county subdivisions by county and normalised name, with hand-checked pairs in assumptions/zoning.yaml.
sources.limits: Self-reported by municipalities and updated when they tell DCED; some entries may be out of date. Says whether an ordinance or plan exists, not what it allows or when it was last revised. DCED ids are matched to Census county subdivisions by name; unmatched names are listed in the build notes.
sources.publisher: Pennsylvania Department of Community and Economic Development (DCED)

sources.source: City and Town Population Totals (subcounty resident population estimates) (U.S. Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program)
sources.cleaning: Keeps county subdivision rows (summary level 061) and the city-county of Philadelphia; the latest year's estimate is used.
sources.limits: Model-based estimates, not counts; small municipalities carry wide error.
sources.publisher: U.S. Census Bureau, Population Estimates Program

sources.source: 2020 Census Block Assignment Files, county subdivisions (U.S. Census Bureau, Geography Division)
sources.cleaning: Only the county subdivision member is read; block and subdivision codes are kept.
sources.limits: Uses 2020 municipal boundaries; later annexations and mergers are not reflected.

sources.source: Philadelphia Properties and Assessment History (opa_properties_public) (City of Philadelphia, Office of Property Assessment (via OpenDataPhilly, Carto SQL))
sources.version: Assessment file as read on the build date (tax year 2027 values at the time of writing)
sources.licence: City of Philadelphia open data; licence to be confirmed before release (only derived totals are kept, and the City is credited)
sources.cleaning: Read in pages on the City's server. Only location (5 decimals), category, value, year built, lot area, last sale and three 0/1 flags (homestead, entity-looking owner name, out-of-state tax-bill address) leave the server; owner names and addresses never do. Parcels are placed in 2020 tracts by outline.
sources.limits: Assessment records, not a census of who lives where. Market values are the City's mass-appraisal estimates. The last sale is the only sale on file, so repeat sales in a window are undercounted. Condominium units are filed as single family and are separated by building description.
sources.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Office of Property Assessment (via OpenDataPhilly, Carto SQL)

sources.source: Philadelphia Real Estate Transfers (rtt_summary) (City of Philadelphia, Department of Records (via OpenDataPhilly, Carto SQL))
sources.version: Transfer records as read on the build date
sources.licence: City of Philadelphia open data; licence to be confirmed before release (only yearly totals are kept)
sources.cleaning: Counted on the City's server per year; only yearly totals are downloaded.
sources.limits: Grantee names are judged entity or person by word list only. The single-family test uses today's property category, not the category on the sale date.
sources.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Department of Records (via OpenDataPhilly, Carto SQL)

sources.source: Philadelphia Licenses and Inspections building permits (permits) (City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections (via OpenDataPhilly, Carto SQL))
sources.version: Permits as read on the build date, issued from 2016
sources.licence: City of Philadelphia open data; licence to be confirmed before release (only tract totals are kept)
sources.cleaning: New-construction building permits only (types in assumptions/pipeline_local.yaml); location, year and homes kept.
sources.limits: Permits issued, not homes started or finished. A record-system change in 2020 renamed permit types; both names are counted. A 2021 rush ahead of a tax abatement change inflates that year.
sources.publisher: City of Philadelphia, Department of Licenses and Inspections (via OpenDataPhilly, Carto SQL)

sources.source: Allegheny County Property Assessments (Allegheny County Office of Property Assessments (via the Western Pennsylvania Regional Data Center))
sources.version: Assessment file as read on the build date (values on the county's 2012 base year)
sources.cleaning: Added up per 2020 tract on WPRDC's server; no names or addresses are downloaded.
sources.limits: Fair market values are 2012 base-year assessments, far below today's prices. The owner type "CORPORATION" is the assessment office's code, not a name test.
sources.publisher: Allegheny County Office of Property Assessments (via the Western Pennsylvania Regional Data Center)

sources.source: Parcel Centroids in Allegheny County with Geographic Identifiers (March 2025) (Western Pennsylvania Regional Data Center)
sources.cleaning: Joined to assessments and sales on the parcel id on WPRDC's server.
sources.limits: Parcels created after March 2025 have no centre point and are counted only in the county total.

sources.source: Allegheny County Real Estate Sales (Allegheny County Office of Property Assessments (via the Western Pennsylvania Regional Data Center))
sources.version: Sales as read on the build date
sources.cleaning: Valid single-family sales counted and their median price taken on WPRDC's server.
sources.limits: Only sales the assessment office marked valid (sale codes in assumptions/parcels.yaml) are counted.
sources.publisher: Allegheny County Office of Property Assessments (via the Western Pennsylvania Regional Data Center)

sources.source: City of Pittsburgh PLI Permits (City of Pittsburgh, Department of Permits, Licenses and Inspections (via WPRDC))
sources.version: Permits as read on the build date (the file starts in mid-2019)
sources.cleaning: Residential new-construction building permits only; location and year kept.
sources.limits: No home counts, so only permits are counted. City of Pittsburgh only, not the rest of Allegheny County.
sources.publisher: City of Pittsburgh, Department of Permits, Licenses and Inspections (via WPRDC)

sources.source: PHFA Low-Income Housing Tax Credit award lists (Pennsylvania Housing Finance Agency (PHFA))
sources.version: Award lists posted on the build date (from 2019; scanned lists are skipped)
sources.licence: Public information published by a Pennsylvania state agency; no licence stated
sources.cleaning: Each PDF is saved to a temporary file and read with pypdf. Name, city, ZIP, county, homes and credit kept; sponsor contacts are never kept.
sources.limits: Awards, not homes built: some awarded projects are delayed or dropped. Read from PDFs whose layout changes yearly; a list with no text layer is skipped. Sites described as intersections or scattered sites have no tract.

sources.source: Census Geocoder (geographies, one-line address) (U.S. Census Bureau)
sources.cleaning: Only the 2020 tract code of the first match is kept.
sources.limits: Street addresses only; intersections and scattered sites are not found.

sources.source: County comprehensive plans (citation list in assumptions/plans.yaml) (Pennsylvania county planning commissions)
sources.licence: Public documents of each county; cited, not copied
sources.cleaning: None; name, adoption year and link are typed from each county's page and marked verified or not.
sources.limits: A citation list for large counties only; each county's own page is the authority.

sources.source: Ownership Profile of Single-Family Residence Properties in Philadelphia: A Focus on Large Corporate Investors (cited benchmark, not ingested) (Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia)
sources.licence: Cited publication; one figure quoted with attribution, no data copied
sources.cleaning: None; the figure and its locator are recorded in assumptions/evidence.yaml (_owners).
sources.limits: Philadelphia only. Large corporate investors are entities with 26 or more parcels; the share is of single-family rentals, not all homes.

sources.source: Single-Family Home Sales in Philadelphia (cited benchmark, not ingested) (The Pew Charitable Trusts)
sources.licence: Cited publication; one figure quoted with attribution, no data copied
sources.cleaning: None; the figure and its locator are recorded in assumptions/evidence.yaml (_owners).
sources.limits: Philadelphia only. Investors include named entities and individuals buying more than two homes; cash buyers are not counted, so it is a floor.
